lines.g1: Go was built at Google for fast servers that handle many things at once.
lines.g2: It compiles to a single binary, so deploying means copying one file.
lines.g3: A goroutine is a function running on its own, and it costs only a few kilobytes.
lines.g4: The runtime schedules thousands of goroutines onto a few operating system threads.
lines.g5: Goroutines talk to each other through channels.
lines.g6: The Go proverb: do not communicate by sharing memory; share memory by communicating.
